Toy list of missing taxa, with allowed states of two traits: biogeographic ranges and elevation

Source: R/dataset_doc.R
toy_missing_taxa_list_with_ranges_and_elevation.Rd

Same as phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list, with the extra item $allowed_states covering the states of two traits, the biogeographic ranges of phylograftR::toy_simmap_ranges ("A", "B", "AB", "BC") and the elevation of phylograftR::toy_simmap_elevation ("high", "low"), in which each taxon can be grafted. It is used to showcase the grafting constrained by a range trait and a 'normal' trait at once, with treat_states_as_ranges = c(biogeo = TRUE, elevation = FALSE) (see the Details section "Biogeographic ranges as states" of phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa()).

It is the output of phylograftR::import_missing_taxa_list() applied to the table system.file("extdata", "toy_missing_taxa_with_ranges_and_elevation.csv", package = "phylograftR"). In the column allowed_states, the states of the traits are separated by semicolons (in the order of the maps provided in simmap: the ranges, then the elevation), and the states of a trait by commas. Open that file to see the different syntaxes:

  • "A;high": the range is "A", and the elevation is "high".

  • "B, BC;": the range is "B" or "BC", and the elevation has no taxon-level value (the global value is used).

  • "elevation=low": traits named, so the ranges can be omitted (they have no taxon-level value).

  • "biogeo=A, BC; elevation=high": all the traits named, in any order.

  • Blank cell: no taxon-level value for any trait, so the global allowed_states argument is used for both.

The names of the traits (biogeo and elevation) must match the names of the maps provided in simmap to use the syntax with names.

Usage

data(toy_missing_taxa_list_with_ranges_and_elevation)

Format

A named list with the same 7 taxa and items as phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list, and the extra item:

  • $allowed_states List (one element per taxon, named after the taxa) of lists with the states of each trait (one element per trait, NULL for a trait without taxon-level value), or NULL to use the global allowed_states argument for all the traits. "New_sp1": list("A", "high"); "New_sp4": list(c("B", "BC"), NULL); "New_sp5": list(elevation = "low"); "New_sp7": list(biogeo = c("A", "BC"), elevation = "high"); the others: NULL.

See also

Other datasets and functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list_with_allowed_ranges for the same missing taxa list, with allowed biogeographic ranges.

  • phylograftR::toy_simmap_ranges for the stochastic character map of biogeographic ranges.

  • phylograftR::toy_simmap_elevation for the stochastic character map of elevation.

  • phylograftR::toy_missing_taxa_list_with_two_traits for the list with allowed states of colors and elevation.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() to graft taxa within a target clade based on ranges and elevation, using this dataset.

toy_missing_taxa_list_with_ranges_and_elevation$allowed_states

system.file("extdata", "toy_missing_taxa_with_ranges_and_elevation.csv", package = "phylograftR")
#> [1] "/home/runner/.cache/R/renv/library/phylograftR-802cedf8/linux-ubuntu-resolute/R-4.6/x86_64-pc-linux-gnu/phylograftR/extdata/toy_missing_taxa_with_ranges_and_elevation.csv"

# Graft with the maps of the two traits. The first trait is treated as ranges,
# the second as 'normal', non-biogeographic states.
# Taxa without taxon-level states can be grafted on branches
# in a range containing "A" or "B" (global value),
# whatever the elevation (NULL).

# Load datasets
data(toy_backbone)
data(toy_simmap_ranges)
data(toy_simmap_elevation)

# Graft with constraints from elevation states and biogeographic ranges
grafted_phy <- graft_missing_taxa(phy = toy_backbone,
    missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list_with_ranges_and_elevation,
    simmap = list(biogeo = toy_simmap_ranges, elevation = toy_simmap_elevation),
    allowed_states = list(c("A", "B"), NULL),
    treat_states_as_ranges = c(biogeo = TRUE, elevation = FALSE),
    verbose = FALSE, seed = 1234)

# Result stores one updated simmap per trait
names(grafted_phy$simmap)
#> [1] "biogeo"    "elevation"

# State of each grafted taxon for each trait: should match the allowed states
taxon_names <- toy_missing_taxa_list_with_ranges_and_elevation$Taxon_name
taxon_states <- sapply(grafted_phy$simmap, function (simmap)
{
  tip_edges <- match(match(taxon_names, simmap$tip.label), simmap$edge[, 2])
  setNames(vapply(simmap$maps[tip_edges], function (x) names(x)[1], character(1)), taxon_names)
})
taxon_states

# Check that all the grafted taxa respect their constraints, trait by trait
check_grafting_constraints(
    phy_grafted = grafted_phy,
    phy_backbone = toy_backbone,
    missing_taxa_list = toy_missing_taxa_list_with_ranges_and_elevation,
    allowed_states = list(c("A", "B"), NULL),
    treat_states_as_ranges = c(biogeo = TRUE, elevation = FALSE))
